STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.claim: The final section again warns against denying God's signs and persisting in idolatry.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.anchor: repeats the warnings about denying the signs of God and persisting in idolatry

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.claim: People receive every favor from God yet thank others and associate partners incapable of benefiting or harming them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.anchor: while they receive all favours from God, they thank and appreciate others. They associate such partners with God who can neither benefit nor harm them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.claim: Idolatry has a conceptual component—the beings taken as God's partners—and a material component—the carved statues thought to embody them and used as worship's vehicles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.anchor: Idol-worship has two components. One, those beings which idol worshippers regard to be partners of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.claim: The Qur’an refutes the statue component: statues cannot fend off a fly or protect offerings from cats and dogs, so they cannot save their worshippers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.anchor: These statues cannot even ward off a fly from their faces and cannot even protect the milk and sweet dishes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.claim: Islahi cites the Psalms as a parallel description of idols as lifeless, with useless senses and limbs, and of their makers and trusting worshippers becoming like them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.anchor: The Psalms point precisely to this aspect in the following words:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p157.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p157.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p157.claim: The command to summon partners and carry out schemes against the Prophet responds to the idolaters' threats.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p157.anchor: “bring all your partners you associate with God; then execute all your schemes against me and do not give me respite” are a response to the warnings of the Idolaters.

STUDYQURAN:7:194/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r2.claim: The rhetorical questions stress that idols lack even human capacities, so it makes no sense to worship beings less capable than their worshippers.
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r2.anchor: How, then, the questions imply, can one worship what is less capable than oneself?

STUDYQURAN:7:194/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r3.claim: The Prophet is told to challenge the idolaters to try their utmost to thwart God and the Prophet's mission.
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r3.anchor: scheme against me, and grant me no respite, is that they try their best to thwart God and the mission of His Prophet

STUDYQURAN:7:194/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r4.claim: Noah and Hūd issue identical or similar challenges to their peoples.
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r4.anchor: This is identical or similar to statements made by Noah and Hūd to their disbelieving peoples

STUDYQURAN:7:194/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r5.claim: The invitation to scheme recalls God's challenge to deniers; their plans cannot thwart Him, while His scheme remains firm despite granting respite.
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r5.anchor: naught in the heavens or upon the earth can thwart God

TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r1.claim: The questions test whether idols can travel to help worshippers, defend and support them, see what is hidden from them, or hear and report what they cannot hear.
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r1.anchor: في حوائجكم ويتصرفون بها في منافعكم

TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r2.claim: The argument is that people revere what they expect to provide benefits through such faculties, so worship of images lacking all these means of gaining benefit or avoiding harm makes no sense.
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r2.anchor: والمعظم من الأشياء إنما يعظم لما يرجى منه من المنافع التي توصل إليه بعض هذه المعاني عندكم

TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r3.claim: In the command to plot, the addressed plural includes the idolaters and their idols.

TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r4.claim: The challenge means do not delay your plotting or trickery; act at once.

TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p635#2/r5.claim: The challenge shows that God protected the Prophet from them and that their idols cannot defend worshippers who seek to harm him.

TABATABAI:7:194-195/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r8.claim: The imagined legs, hands, eyes, and ears of the idols do not walk, grasp, see, or hear, because the idols are inanimate.
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r8.anchor: وليست ما عبأتم لهم من الأرجل والأيدي ماشية وباطشة

TABATABAI:7:194-195/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r10.claim: The Prophet is told to challenge the idolaters and their partners to attack him, showing that God, who revealed the guiding Book and protects the righteous, grants him victory while idols lack knowledge and power.
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r10.anchor: ثم أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يكر عليهم على انتصارهم بأربابهم وآلهتهم بالتحدي والإعجاز

TABATABAI:7:194-195/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r11.claim: The author links the Prophet’s expected protection to God’s promise that His righteous servants inherit the earth and to Muhammad’s declaration that he is among the righteous.
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r11.anchor: وهو القائل إن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون وأنا من الصالحين فينصرني ولا محالة

TABATABAI:7:194-195/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r12.claim: The challenge to idols and their worshippers is presented as one made by other prophets as well.
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r12.anchor: ثم أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يكر عليهم على انتصارهم بأربابهم وآلهتهم بالتحدي والإعجاز

TABATABAI:7:194-195/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r13.claim: The author notes that elsewhere in the Qur’an prophets are not described as declaring their own righteousness in the way Muhammad is here.
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r13.anchor: وفي الآيات أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يخبرهم أنه من الصالحين ولم يعهد فيما يخبر به القرآن من صلاح الأنبياء مثل ذلك في غيره

TABRISI:7:194-195/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:7:194-195/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar alone reads the verb with a damma on ṭāʾ here and in al-Qasas and al-Dukhan; the others use kasra.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وحده يبطشون ههنا وفي القصص والدخان بضم الطاء والباقون بكسرها

TABRISI:7:194-195/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r2.speaker: هشام ويعقوب وأبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وإسماعيل
TABRISI:7:194-195/r2.claim: Hisham and Yaqub retain the yāʾ of kaydūnī in pause and connection; Abu Jaʿfar, Abu ʿAmr, and Ismaʿil agree in connection only, while the rest omit it in both.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r2.anchor: قرأ هشام ويعقوب كيدوني بياء في الوقف والوصل ووافقهما أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وإسماعيل في الوصل

TABRISI:7:194-195/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r3.speaker: يعقوب
TABRISI:7:194-195/r3.claim: Yaqub reads tanẓirūnī with the yāʾ in both pause and connection.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r3.anchor: وقرأ تنظروني بالياء في الحالين يعقوب

TABRISI:7:194-195/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:7:194-195/r4.claim: Both yabṭishu and yabṭushu are Arabic forms, though the kasra form is more eloquent.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r4.anchor: بطش يبطش ويبطش والكسر أفصح وقال أبو علي

TABRISI:7:194-195/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:7:194-195/r5.claim: Clause endings work like poetic rhyme because both mark the end; rhyme may require dropping a final yāʾ, as illustrated by al-Aʿsha and another verse of poetry.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r5.anchor: الفواصل من الكلام التام تجري مجرى القوافي لاجتماعهما في أن الفاصلة آخر الآية كما أن القافية آخر البيت

TABRISI:7:194-195/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:194-195/r13.claim: The rhetorical questions deny that idols have limbs or senses with which to walk, defend worshippers, see, or hear; people have these faculties and surpass idols.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r13.anchor: أي ليس لهم هذه الحواس ولكم هذه الحواس فأنتم أفضل منهم فلو دعوتم وعبدتم من له الحياة

TABRISI:7:194-195/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:194-195/r14.claim: Even worshipping a living being with useful faculties would merit blame, since it too is created and governed by God.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r14.anchor: للزمكم الذم واللوم بذلك لأنها مخلوقة مربوبة فكيف تعبدون من أنتم أفضل منه

TABRISI:7:194-195/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:194-195/r15.claim: Muhammad challenges the polytheists to gather with their supposed partners and plot without delay; his God protects him, while their idols cannot protect them.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r15.anchor: ومعناه أن معبودي ينصرني ويدفع كيد الكائدين عني ومعبودكم لا يقدر على نصركم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the challenge asks whether the idols have legs and hands like living human beings, capable of walking and grasping.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: مثل بني آدم ممن جعلت فيه الروح. {أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r2.claim: بطش means seizing during an assault or forcefully taking hold of anything; 85:12 uses the same root.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r2.anchor: ومعنى البطش (¬3): التناول عند الصولة، والأخذ الشديد في كل شيء: بطش،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r3.claim: The people of meaning say worshipping bodies plainly unable to harm or benefit is especially foolish: humans have limbs the idols lack, so the worshippers are superior to their gods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p531/r3.anchor: قال أهل المعاني في هذه الآية: (إنما أنكر عليهم عبادة من لا رجل له يمشي بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the partners as those worshipped besides God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2): (يريد: الذين تعبدون (¬3) من دون الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r2.claim: The challenge completes the preceding proof: those worshipping beings without power cannot protect them, whereas God controls harm and benefit and their plotting cannot harm Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r2.anchor: وهذا يتصل بما قبله اتصال استكمال الحجة عليهم؛ لأنهم لما فزعوا بعبادة من لا يملك ضرا ولا نفعا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the idolaters used to threaten Muhammad with their gods, so God told him to challenge them to plot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r3.anchor: قال الحسن (¬4): (إنهم كانوا يخوفونه بآلهتهم فقال الله تعالى: {قل ادعوا شركاءكم ثم كيدون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r4.claim: Readers transmit both retaining and omitting the yāʾ in كيدون and فلا تنظرون.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في إثبات الياء (¬5) في {كيدون} وحذفها، فقرءوا بالوجهين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r5.claim: Verse endings act like poetic rhymes, which can license dropping these final yāʾ letters; the cited poetry illustrates deletion, while retention follows the original form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r5.anchor: والقول في ذلك أن الفواصل وما أشبه الفواصل من الكلام التام تجري مجرى القوافي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r6.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r6.claim: The cited poem illustrates a final yāʾ omitted at a rhyme, in the form يأتين.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r6.anchor: فهل يمنعني ارتيادي البلاد ... من قدر الموت أن يأتين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r7.claim: فلا تنظرون means do not delay me; hasten your plotting against me and your partners.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r7.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {فلا تنظرون}. أي: لا تمهلوني واعجلوا في كيدي أنتم وشركاؤكم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r8.claim: This verse supports the صاحب النظم's interpretation of 7:194 by explaining that humans surpass the idols in bodily powers, so the idols cannot truly be their equals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p532/r8.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على صحة ما قال صاحب النظم في الآية الأولى، ألا ترى أنه بين فضل الآدمي على الأصنام

QASHANI:7:195-198/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:195-198/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:195-198/r1.claim: The question is a denial: although idols have limbs, they do not move independently; God moves them, as with all other organs.
QASHANI:7:195-198/r1.anchor: استفهام على سبيل الإنكار، أي: ألهم أرجل ولكن لا يمشون بها

QASHANI:7:195-198/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:195-198/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:195-198/r4.claim: The Prophet challenges the jinn and human partners to scheme against him, confident that God protects him.
QASHANI:7:195-198/r4.anchor: من الجن والإنس { ثم كيدون } إن استطعتم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r4.claim: The questions contrast idols with human beings, who can walk and grasp with their limbs.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r4.anchor: مشي بني آدم { أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها } يتناولون بها مثل بطش بني آدم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r5.claim: The idols also lack the sight and hearing that human beings possess.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r5.anchor: أم لهم أعين يبصرون بها أم لهم آذان يسمعون بها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r6.claim: The Prophet challenges the polytheists and their partners to plot against him without delay.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r6.anchor: الذين تعبدون من دون الله { ثم كيدون } أنتم وشركاؤكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r7.claim: They are told not to give him respite, but to hurry in plotting against him.

ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r1.claim: The Prophet challenges the polytheists to summon all their partners and plot against him without delay, showing that he fears no harm from them.
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r1.anchor: Haydi bütün şerîklerinizi çağırınız {ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ فَلَا تُنظِرُونِ} sonra hepiniz bana ne hile kurabilirseniz

ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r7.speaker: Keşşâf gibi بعض müfessîrin
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r7.claim: To avoid apparent repetition, those commentators distinguished the first passage as a reproach and this one as separating what may from what may not be worshipped.
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r7.anchor: Keşşâf gibi bazı müfessîrin bu beyânâtın da evvelki gibi yalnız esnâma dair olduğuna zâhib olmuşlar

ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r8.claim: Elmalılı rejects the repetition argument: the first passage addresses inanimate idols, while this one concerns the leaders whom the polytheists worship.
ELMALILI:7:190-198#2/r8.anchor: Fakat doğrusu âyette asla tekrar yoktur. Çünkü müşriklerin şürekâsı sade câmid putlardan ibaret değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r4.claim: Everything worshipped as divine by Arab idolaters or polytheists throughout history is created by God, and there is no deity besides Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r4.anchor: gerek Arap putperestlerinin gerekse tarihin bütün dönemlerindeki müşriklerin tanrısal nitelikler yükleyerek şu veya bu şekilde taptıkları her şey Allah’ın yaratıklarıdır; “O’ndan başka tanrı yoktur.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r5.claim: The objects are inanimate, unconscious, and ignorant; they lack divine qualities, cannot guide others, and cannot even hear a call directed to them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r5.anchor: o cansız, şuursuz ve bilgisiz nesneler kendilerine yapılacak çağrıyı bile duyma yeteneğinden yoksundurlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r7.claim: The rhetorical challenge shows the irrationality of worshipping objects less capable and more defective than humans, lacking even ordinary limbs and senses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r7.anchor: sıradan bir canlıda bulunan yürüyecek ayağa, tutacak ele, görecek göze bile sahip olmayan bu nesneleri tanrı tanımak; insanların

QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r1.claim: The idols lack the bodily capacities and praiseworthy qualities their worshipers possess; it is incoherent to worship what is even more deficient than they are.
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r1.anchor: بين بهذه الآيات أن الأصنام التي عبدوها دونهم فيما اعتقدوا فيه صفة المدح

QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r2.claim: Knowing that the deity can guide and answer its petitioner makes the servant renounce personal power and single out God as able to meet needs and remove distress, cutting hope in creatures.
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r2.anchor: وعلم العبد بقدرة معبوده يوجب تبريه عن حوله وقوته ، وإفراد الحق - سبحانه - بالقدرة على قضاء حاجته

QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r3.claim: True reliance on God means not caring about anything besides Him, since He alone controls benefit, harm, good, and evil.
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r3.anchor: صدق التوكل على الله يوجب ترك المبالاة بغير الله

QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r4.claim: Whoever fulfills God’s due is cared for sufficiently by Him; God directs the servant’s affairs with grace, and if He withholds a desired outcome, makes the servant content with what He does.
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r4.anchor: من قام بحق الله تولى أموره على وجه الكفاية ، فلا يخرجه إلى مثاله

QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r5.claim: The spirit of contentment bestowed on the innermost secrets is fuller than the comfort of receiving gifts in the heart.
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r5.anchor: وروح الرضا على الأسرار أتم من راحة العطاء على القلوب

QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r6.claim: Although idolaters saw their idols with their physical eyes, their inner hearts and secrets were veiled from true sight, so their seeing did not count.
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r6.anchor: شاهدوه بأبصارهم لكنهم حجبوا عن رؤيته ببصائر أسرارهم وقلوبهم فلم يعتد برؤيتهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r7.claim: Seeing spiritual masters is not seeing their bodies; it is the heart’s unveiling of the unseen, in proportion to reverence and faith.
QUSHAYRI:v1p373/r7.anchor: رؤية الأكابر ليست بشهود أشخاصهم ، لكن بما يحصل للقلوب من مكاشفات الغيب

BURHAN:v3p399/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p399/r1.speaker: ابن المنير
BURHAN:v3p399/r1.claim: Ibn al-Munīr rejects the correction made by al-Aṣmaʿī, Khalaf al-Aḥmar, and Ibn Rashīq, and says Jarīr was right: his line meant a day of good without any evil; before can itself negate.
BURHAN:v3p399/r1.anchor: قال ابن المنير ووقع لي أن الأصمعي وخلف الأحمر وابن رشيق أخطئوا جميعا وأصاب جرير وحده

BURHAN:v3p399/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p399/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p399/r2.claim: The passage illustrates denying a necessary concomitant to deny its subject: the rhetorical questions about idols’ eyes and ears in fact deny that they possess the organs at all.
BURHAN:v3p399/r2.anchor: فإن ظاهره نفي هذه الجوارح والحقيقة توجب نفي الآية عمن يكون له فضلا عمن لا يكون

BURHAN:v3p270/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p270/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p270/r1.claim: The verse escalates from legs to hands to eyes to ears because the later faculties have greater or broader benefits, with hearing highest in importance.
BURHAN:v3p270/r1.anchor: الترقي كقوله ﴿ ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد

BURHAN:v3p270/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p270/r3.speaker: الشيخ أبو الفتح القشيري
BURHAN:v3p270/r3.claim: Abu al-Fath al-Qushayri objects that denying the highest attribute first and then lesser ones would intensify the blame, since denying the highest does not entail denying the rest.
BURHAN:v3p270/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو الفتح القشيري فإن قيل قد كان الأولى أن يقدم الوصف الأعلى

BURHAN:v3p270/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p270/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p270/r4.claim: The author answers that the sequence first establishes idols as like their worshippers in being created and subdued, then removes shared attributes from weaker to stronger until all resemblance disappears; this is subtler.
BURHAN:v3p270/r4.anchor: والمقصود من الآية طريقة أخرى وهي أنه تعالى أثبت أن الأصنام التي تعبدها الكفار

BURHAN:v4p56/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p56/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p56/r4.claim: من is used for idols, although ما is normal for nonrational things, because the audience treats the idols as deities; the author answers that the wording aims to make the intended target clear to them.
BURHAN:v4p56/r4.anchor: وكان أصله كما لايخلق لأن ما لمن لايعقل بخلاف من

ITQAN:v1p123/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p123/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ITQAN:v1p123/r4.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri taught the Qurʾan five verses at dawn and five at dusk and said Gabriel brought it down five at a time.
ITQAN:v1p123/r4.anchor: وأخرجه ابن عساكر من طريق أبي نضرة قال كان أبو سعيد الخدري يعلمنا القرآن خمس آيات بالغداة وخمس آيات بالعشي ويخبر أن جبريل نزل بالقرآن خمس آيات خمس آيات

ITQAN:v1p123/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p123/r5.speaker: عمر
ITQAN:v1p123/r5.claim: A report from Umar says to learn five verses at a time because Gabriel descended with five; a weak report from Ali adds that this protects memory except for al-Anʿam.
ITQAN:v1p123/r5.anchor: وأما ما أخرجه البيهقي في الشعب من طريق أبي خلدة عن عمر قال تعلموا القرآن خمس آيات خمس آيات فإن جبريل كان ينزل بالقرآن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خمسا خمسا ومن طريق ضعيف عن علي

ITQAN:v1p123/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p123/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p123/r6.claim: If the five-at-a-time report is sound, it means Gabriel conveyed five verses for the Prophet to memorize before giving him the remainder, not that revelation always came exclusively in five-verse units.
ITQAN:v1p123/r6.anchor: فالجواب أن معناه إن صح إلقاؤه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذا القدر حتى يحفظه ثم يلقى إليه الباقي لا إنزاله بهذا القدر خاصة

ITQAN:v1p123/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p123/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
ITQAN:v1p123/r7.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya likewise tells students to learn five verses at a time, saying the Prophet received them from Gabriel in groups of five.
ITQAN:v1p123/r7.anchor: ما أخرجه البيهقي أيضا عن خالد بن دينار قال قال لنا أبو العالية تعلموا القرآن خمس آيات خمس آيات فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يأخذه من جبريل خمسا خمسا

ITQAN:v1p123/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p123/r8.speaker: الأصفهاني
ITQAN:v1p123/r8.claim: Al-Isfahani says Sunnis agree that God's speech is revealed but differ over what “revelation” means: either manifestation of its recitation or God's teaching the words to Gabriel in heaven for delivery on earth.
ITQAN:v1p123/r8.anchor: قال الأصفهاني في أوائل تفسيره اتفق أهل السنة والجماعة على أن كلام الله منزل واختلفوا في معنى الإنزال فمنهم من قال إظهار القراءة ومنهم من قال إن الله تعالى ألهم كلامه جبريل

ITQAN:v1p123/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p123/r9.speaker: الأصفهاني
ITQAN:v1p123/r9.claim: Al-Isfahani describes two modes of transmission: the Prophet rises from human to angelic form and receives from Gabriel, or the angel descends to human form; he calls the first harder.
ITQAN:v1p123/r9.anchor: وفي التنزيل طريقان أحدهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انخلع من صورة البشرية إلى صورة الملكية وأخذه من جبريل والثاني أن الملك انخلع إلى البشرية حتى يأخذه الرسول منه والأول أصعب الحالين

ITQAN:v2p445#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p445#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p445#3/r1.claim: In this verse أم is disconnected because it follows a hamza of repudiation, which functions like negation; connected أم does not follow negation.

ITQAN:v2p445#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p445#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p445#3/r2.claim: Disconnected أم always signals a shift or transition; sometimes it only shifts the discourse, and sometimes it adds a rhetorical question of denial.
ITQAN:v2p445#3/r2.anchor: ومعنى أم المنقطعة الذي لا يفارقها الإضراب ثم تارة تكون له مجردا وتارة تضمن مع ذلك استفهاما إنكاريا

ITQAN:v3p39/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p39/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p39/r1.claim: The verse ascends from lower to higher faculties: feet, then hands, then eyes, then hearing, since each later faculty is nobler than the previous one.
ITQAN:v3p39/r1.anchor: بدأ بالأدنى لغرض الترقي لأن اليد أشرف من الرجل والعين أشرف من اليد والسمع أشرف من البصر

ITQAN:v3p39/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p39/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p39/r5.claim: Other reasons for ordering include preserving verse endings and producing restriction or exclusivity; the author says many further examples will follow.
ITQAN:v3p39/r5.anchor: ومنها رعاية الفواصل وسيأتي لذلك أمثلة كثيرة ومنها أفادة الحصر للاختصاص وسيأتي في النوع الخامس والخمسين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r1.claim: Abbas ibn al-Ahnaf aptly uses pouring tears as a sign of grief, since crying conventionally signals sorrow, as do the idioms and the cited line about time making one cry or laugh.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r1.anchor: إلى قول العباس بن الأحنف ، من + الطويل + : ( سأطلب بعد الدار عنكم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r2.claim: The poem's wish that the eyes become dry cannot signal reunion's joy: الجمود means an eye fails to weep when grief calls for tears, so the condition is a defect and complaint.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r2.anchor: ألا إن عينا لم تجد يوم واسط عليك بجاري دمعها لجمود

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r3.claim: The language calls an eye without tears, a year without rain, and a she-camel without milk جماد, each suggesting withholding or barrenness rather than happiness.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p208/r3.anchor: عين جمود ؛ لا ماء فيها ، وسنة جماد ؛ لا مطر فيها ، وناقة جماد ؛ لا لبن فيها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r1.claim: A person can be eager only for what is not yet present; desire cannot properly target what already exists or what is past.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r1.anchor: وإنما يكون الحرص على ما لم يوجد بعد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r2.claim: Life is indefinite in لكم في القصاص حياة because the point is life gained for some future portion through deterrence, not life itself or life in every period; the same partial benefit explains فيه شفاء للناس.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r2.anchor: وإذا كان المعنى على حياة في بعض أوقاته وجب التنكير ، وامتنع التعريف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r3.claim: The person deterred from murder is not the one whose life is saved by qisas; qisas saves the intended victim who otherwise would be killed, further restricting the meaning to a subset.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p223/r3.anchor: هذه الحياة إنما هي لمن كان يقتل لولا القصاص

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r1.claim: An unattributed verse assigns gifts across the lands of Najd and the lowlands to one generous benefactor.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r1.anchor: ففي كل نجد في البلاد وغائر مواهب ليست منه وهي مواهبه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r2.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's inaccessible beloved who entices beneath her veil is paired with al-Buhturi's woman who arouses hope, then turns away and disappoints.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r2.anchor: قول المتنبي ، + البسيط + : ( بيضاء تطمع فيما تحت حلتها وعز ذلك مطلوبا إذا طلبا )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r3.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's wish to be remembered by one who will not translate his desire parallels Abu Tammam's paradox of gaining glory by forgoing pursuit.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r3.anchor: وقول المتنبي ، + الكامل + : ( إذكار مثلك ترك إذكاري له إذ لا تريد لما أريد مترجما )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r4.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's sunlike woman appears when veiled, echoing Qays ibn al-Khatim's wish that God made her impossible to veil.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r4.anchor: وقول أبي تمام ، + الكامل + : ( فنعمت من شمس إذا حجبت بدت من خدرها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r5.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's eyelashes wound hearts before skin, paralleling Kathir's arrow-like glance that leaves the skin untouched but wounds the heart.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r5.anchor: وقول المتنبي ، + الخفيف + : ( راميات بأسهم ريشها الهدب تشق القلوب قبل الجلود )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r6.claim: A verse attributed to Labid makes safety itself a disease, while Abu al-Atahiya says a person's perfection hastens his decline.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r6.anchor: ويعزى إلى لبيد ، + الكامل + : ( ودعوت ربي بالسلامة جاهدا ليصحني فإذا السلامة داء )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r7.claim: Abu al-Atahiya says a lover's visits should be reduced so affection stays fresh; Abu Tammam similarly says a long stay wears one down and travel renews.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r7.anchor: وقوله ، + مجزوء الكامل + : ( أقلل زيارتك الحبيب تكون كالثوب استجده )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r8.claim: Al-Khuraymi says his benefactor underestimates a kindness celebrated by others; al-Mutanabbi says people mistake the addressee's absence for their own good fortune.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r8.anchor: وقول الخريمي ، + الرمل + : ( زاد معروفك عندي عظما أنه عندك محقور صغير )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r9.claim: Al-Buhturi observes that calamities target people of virtue; al-Mutanabbi similarly says the age targets the best people, leaving the least perceptive free of worry.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p358/r9.anchor: وقول البحتري ، + الوافر + : ( ألم تر للنوائب كيف تسمو إلى أهل النوافل والفضول ؟ )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r1.claim: In the example شر أهر ذا ناب, شر remains an indefinite from its genus; the point is that the one who made the tusked creature roar belongs to evil rather than good.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r1.anchor: الغرض من الكلام أن نبين أن الذي أهر ذا الناب هو من جنس الشر لا جنس الخير

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r2.claim: In أرجل أتاك أم امرأة, the question concerns the visitor’s gender or kind; in أرجل أتاك أم رجلان, it instead asks whether one or two came.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r2.anchor: وعكس هذا أنك إذا قلت : أرجل أتاك أم رجلان ؟ كان القصد منك إلى كونه واحدا دون كونه رجلا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r3.claim: A noun’s form may indicate more than one thing, while the speaker intends only one implication; the unselected implication is effectively outside the utterance’s intended meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p120/r3.anchor: فإذا بدأت بالنكرة فقلت : رجل ، وأنت لا تقصد بها الجنس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r1.claim: Repeating Imruʾ al-Qays’s poem does not make its reciter a poet or an imitator: the words were not first created by the reciter, just as shaping a shoe to a model makes one a shoe-cutter.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r1.anchor: كما أن الذي يحذو النعل بالنعل يكون قاطع نعل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r2.claim: If Qurʾānic likeness means reproducing its sequence with different words, sequence must serve a purpose in arranging distinct elements; the challenger must identify the meanings that require that order.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r2.anchor: أعلمت أنه لا يكون الإتيان بالأشياء بعضها في إثر بعض على التوالي نسقا وترتيبا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r3.claim: The appeal to meter cannot explain inimitability in eloquence: meter is not eloquence, and making the Qurʾān miraculous only by weight denies that its speech has an advantage as discourse.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p341/r3.anchor: لأن الوزن ليس هو من الفصاحة والبلاغة في شيء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r1.claim: ʿAyn is a polysemous noun whose primary sense is the seeing eye; customary usage transfers it to other referents.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r1.anchor: العين : من الأسماء المشتركة ، والأصل فيها : العين الباصرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r2.claim: Other lexical uses include a person's very self, springs, visible water, and tribal notables.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r3.claim: ʿAmda ʿayn means deliberate action; ʿabd ʿayn serves only while watched.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r3.anchor: ويقال : أفعل ذلك عمد عين ، إذا تعمده . وهذا عبد عين أي : يخدمك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r4.claim: The source records expressions for meeting someone directly and striking someone with the evil eye.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r4.anchor: ويقال : لقيت فلانا عين عنه ، أي : أعيانا ، ويقال : عنت الرجل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r5.claim: The Qur'anic sense can be the physical, seeing eye.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p443/r5.anchor: أحدها : العين الباصرة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r1.claim: An unnamed poet leaves the second alternative unstated after أهم هممته; Ibn Qutayba cites the line as ellipsis.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r2.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r2.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb's question أرشد طلابها omits the alternative أم غي, supplied by Ibn Qutayba.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r2.anchor: أبو ذؤيب : عصيت إليها القلب إني لأمره

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r6.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r6.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line means that when night came, the donkeys raised their ears; أقبل is omitted before الليل.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r7.claim: An unnamed poet's أن لا إلى أم سالم omits سبيل, meaning there is no way to reach Umm Salim.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r7.anchor: وقد بدا لذي نهية أن لا إلى أم سالم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r9.speaker: النمر بن تولب
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r9.claim: In al-Namir b. Tawlab's line, أينما omits ذهب: wherever the person goes, he will encounter the feared thing.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r9.anchor: النمر بن تولب : فإن المنبه من يخشها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r15.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r15.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r15.claim: An unnamed poet's رأتني بحبليها omits مقبلا: she saw me approaching with the two ropes.

NAHHAS:v2p169/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p169/r1.claim: Humans are better than powerless idols, so the question asks how they can find or call on them.
NAHHAS:v2p169/r1.anchor: أي أنتم أفضل منهم فكيف تجدونهم

NAHHAS:v2p169/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة
NAHHAS:v2p169/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Shayba read ayd as a dialect form; the author notes that hand, foot, and ear are feminine and take feminine hāʾ in diminutives, while yad restores a yāʾ in its diminutive.
NAHHAS:v2p169/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ( أم لهم أيد يبطشون ) وهي لغة

NAHHAS:v2p169/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p169/r3.claim: The partners are those associated with God and assigned a portion of people’s wealth.
NAHHAS:v2p169/r3.anchor: ( قل ادعوا شركاءكم ) أي الذين شركتموهم فجعلتم لهم قسطا

NAHHAS:v2p169/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p169/r4.claim: The original kīdūnī loses its yāʾ, with kasra signaling the omitted letter; likewise fa-lā tunẓirūn means ‘do not delay me.’
NAHHAS:v2p169/r4.anchor: ( ثم كيدون ) والأصل كيدوني بالياء حذفت الياء

SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r1.claim: The common reading has kasra on the ط of يبطشون; Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, and Nāfiʿ in one transmission read it with ḍamma, two dialect forms of بطش, which means to seize forcefully.
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع في رواية عنه: " يبطشون " بضمها وهما لغتان

SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr retains the yāʾ of كيدوني in connection but drops it at pause; Hishām retains it in both positions, with a reported disagreement, while other readers drop it in both.
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو: " كيدوني " بإثبات الياء وصلا وحذفها وقفا. وهشام بإثباتها في الحالين

SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r3.claim: Al-Samīn corrects the Shaykh's report that Abū ʿAmr retains the yāʾ at pause: Abū ʿAmr never retains it there under his rule for extra yāʾs.
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r3.anchor: قلت: أبو عمرو لا يثبتها وقفا البتة، فإن قاعدته [في] الياءات الزائدة

SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r4.claim: Al-Samīn compares the three كيدوني forms: all retain yāʾ in both positions in 11:55, all drop it in both in 77:39, paralleling forms of واخشوني in 2:150 and al-Māʾida.
SAMIN-DURR:7:195/r4.anchor: وفي القراءة " فكيدوني " ثلاثة ألفاظ: هذه وقد عرف حكمها، وفي هود [الآية: 55]

ASAD-NOTES:7:191#n160/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:191#n160/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:191#n160/r1.claim: Asad glosses the summons as calling upon the supposed divine partners and refers to 6:22, note 15.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f1.claim: The Araf passage describes the worshipped idols as lifeless: they cannot create, help, hear, see, move, or do anything, in contrast with God's hearing and knowledge.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f1.anchor: وصف آلهتهم بأنها لا تسمع ولا تبصر ولا تتحرك ولا تقدر على شيء مما يدل على أنها ليس فيها شيء من الحياة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r1.claim: The fully pronounced first-person yā form recurs in its surah more than the shortened form recurs in its own context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r1.anchor: وقد تتردد الكلمة ذات الياء المظهرة في السورة أكثر من تردد الكلمة ذات الياء المجتزأة في موطنها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r2.claim: Hud’s passage is an intense confrontation, so Hud openly presents himself as challenger; Araf lacks that same setting.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r2.anchor: فإن المقام في هود مقام تحدٍّ كبير ومواجهة، فأظهر نفسه زيادة في التحدي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r4.claim: Hud’s challenge and confrontation are longer than Araf’s; the longer yā form suits Hud, while the shortened form suits Araf’s briefer context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r4.anchor: إن التحدي والمواجهة في هود أطول وأكثر مما في الأعراف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.claim: Hud repeatedly uses the first-person yā in this passage, whereas Araf shows it only once, in “Indeed, my protector is Allah”; this repetition suits Hud.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.anchor: ومن ناحية أخرى نرى أنه قد تردد ذكر ياء الضمير في هود في هذا الموطن مرات عديدة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r6.claim: Araf places then before the challenge and fa before denying respite; Hud reverses them. Fa signals immediacy, then delay.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r6.anchor: والفاء تفيد التعقيب أما (ثم) فتفيد التراخي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r7.claim: The immediate denial of respite fits Araf’s early emphasis on swift worldly punishment, while Hud’s context stresses respite and delayed punishment.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r7.anchor: وعدم الإنظار هو المناسب لسياق الأعراف، فقد ذكر في هذه السورة تعجيل العقوبات لمستحقيها في الدنيا

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r8.claim: Araf 7:95 parallels the challenge: “then” marks the period of respite, and fa marks the sudden taking, matching “do plot, then give me no respite.”
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r8.anchor: فالاستدراج المذكور في الآية وهو قوله: {ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا مَكَانَ السيئة الحسنة}

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r9.claim: Araf’s Noah story is concise and moves directly from denial to rescue and drowning; Hud’s longer exchange lets Noah’s people demand the promised punishment and await it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r9.anchor: أما في هود فالكلام طويل وهناك مهلة حتى استبطؤوا ما وعدهم به

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r10.claim: Araf’s account of ʿĀd presents their punishment swiftly, while Hud gives a fuller account after the divine command, including their worldly curse and fate on Judgment Day.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r10.anchor: فانظر كيف عجّل العقوبة لهم في الأعراف فجاء بالفاء الدالة على عدم الإمهال، بخلاف ما في سورة هود

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r11.claim: Araf says the earthquake seized Ṣāliḥ’s people with fa, showing swift punishment; Hud describes their rescue and says the wrongdoers were seized without that fa sequence.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r11.anchor: فذكر إنزال العقوبة بالفاء في الأعراف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r12.claim: Where Araf combines then and fa, then comes first; in Hud the order is reversed, as in the cited challenge and other examples.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r12.anchor: وهنالك أمر فني آخر، وهو أنه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r1.claim: The topic covers omitted letters, verbs, or nouns that would normally be present, and also features stated in one context but omitted in a similar one when context calls for it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r1.anchor: يدخل في هذا الموضوع ما حذف وأصله أن يذكر، كحذف حرف أو فعل أو اسم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r16.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r16.claim: As a general rule, when the yāʾ is written out the context is extended and detailed; where kasra stands in for it, the expression is concise, apart from verse endings and vocatives.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r16.anchor: أن الاجتزاء بالكسرة عن الياء يختلف عن ذكر الياء في كل ما ورد في القرآن الكريم عدا خواتم الآي والنداء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r17.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r17.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r17.claim: He adds that the yāʾ is audibly repeated more often in places where it is written than in places where kasra replaces it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r17.anchor: ومن ناحية أخرى إن الياء تتردد مُظهرةً في المواطن التي تذكر فيها الياء أكثر من المواطن التي يجتزأ بالكسرة عنها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p815/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p815/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p815/r1.claim: Thumma is not restricted to declarative or imperative constructions; Qur’anic examples occur in both.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p815/r1.anchor: (ثم) ليست مختصة بأسلوب إنشائي أو خبري وقد وردت في القرآن الكريم في مواضع كثيرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p815/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p815/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p815/r2.claim: Thumma may order statements in the report without marking later events in time, as shown by verses where God is always witness and by the cited poem.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p815/r2.anchor: قد تكون لمجرد الترتيب في الإخبار (ثم) تفيد الترتيب والتراخي وهذا هو الذي يثيره النحاة

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، وعاصم، وابن عامر، وحمزة، والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi omit the yāʾ in both connected and paused forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: ثم كيدون [الأعراف/ 195] بغير ياء في الوصل والوقف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r2.claim: Abu Amr and Nafi, in the named transmissions, retain yāʾ when connecting the word.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونافع في رواية ابن جماز وإسماعيل بن جعفر بالياء في الوصل

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r3.claim: The text also records Ibn Amir in the transmissions of Warsh, Qalun, and al-Musayyibi without yāʾ in either connection or pause.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r3.anchor: وكذلك ابن عامر في رواية ورش وقالون والمسيبي بغير ياء في وصل ولا وقف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r4.speaker: ابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r4.claim: Al-Farisi’s book has Ibn Dhakwan’s Ibn Amir transmission with yāʾ, while his memory has it without; Ahmad ibn Yusuf reported the latter through Ibn Dhakwan.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r4.anchor: وفي كتابي عن ابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر: ثم كيدوني بياء، وحفظي بغير ياء. كذا حدثني أحمد بن يوسف بإسناده عن ابن ذكوان .

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r5.claim: Deleting final yāʾ at an ayah ending follows the treatment of rhyme endings, where poets also omit yāʾ when the meter remains complete.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r5.anchor: القول في ذلك أن الفواصل وما أشبه الفواصل من الكلام التام تجري مجرى القوافي لاجتماعهما في أن الفاصلة آخر الآية، كما أن القافية آخر البيت

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r6.claim: Retaining yāʾ follows the underlying form and is also attested in poetry, even where the meter works without it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p114#2/r6.anchor: ومن أثبت فلأن الأصل الإثبات، وقد جاء الإثبات في هذا النحو في القوافي أيضا كقوله : وهم أصحاب يوم عكاظ إني

IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r2.claim: These readers omit final yāʾ in ثم كيدون in connection and pause.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ ثم كيدون ﴾ بغير ياء فى الوصل والوقف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع عن ابن جماز وإسماعيل بن جعفر وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r3.claim: Abu ʿAmr, two transmitters from Nafi, and Ibn ʿĀmir are reported with yāʾ in connected reading; Warsh, Qālūn, and al-Musayyibī from Nafi omit it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونافع فى رواية ابن جماز وإسماعيل بن جعفر بالياء فى الوصل وكذلك ابن عامر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r4.claim: Abu Bakr's book reports Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir with yāʾ; Ibn Dhakwān's written reading has it but his memorized one omits it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r4.anchor: وفى كتابى عن ابن ذكوان بإسناده عن ابن عامر ﴿ ثم كيدون ﴾ بياء وقال ابن ذكوان فى كتابى

NASHR:v2p274/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p274/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو جعفر والداجوني عن هشام
NASHR:v2p274/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, and al-Dājūnī from Hishām retain the extra yāʾ in ثم كيدون in connected reading.
NASHR:v2p274/r9.anchor: ثم كيدون أثبتها في الوصل أبو عمرو وأبو جعفر والداجوني عن هشام

NASHR:v2p274/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p274/r10.speaker: يعقوب والحلواني عن هشام
NASHR:v2p274/r10.claim: Yaʿqūb and al-Ḥulwānī from Hishām retain the extra yāʾ in ثم كيدون both in connection and at pause.
NASHR:v2p274/r10.anchor: وأثبتها في الحالين يعقوب والحلواني عن هشام

NASHR:v2p274/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p274/r11.speaker: قنبل من طريق ابن شنبوذ
NASHR:v2p274/r11.claim: Qunbul’s transmission through Ibn Shanabūdh is also reported to retain the yāʾ in ثم كيدون.
NASHR:v2p274/r11.anchor: ورويت عن قنبل من طريق ابن شنبوذ كما تقدم

NASHR:v2p274/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p274/r12.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p274/r12.claim: Yaʿqūb retains the extra yāʾ in تنظرون both in connected reading and at pause.

NASHR:v2p273/r17.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r17.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p273/r17.claim: Abu Jafar reads the ṭāʾ with ḍamma in all three forms of the root.
NASHR:v2p273/r17.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بضم الطاء في الثلاثة

NASHR:v2p273/r18.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r18.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p273/r18.claim: The remaining readers read the ṭāʾ with kasra in all three forms.

NASHR:v2p184/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p184/r4.speaker: أبو نشيط عن أبي جعفر
NASHR:v2p184/r4.claim: Al-Mubhij uniquely reports Abu Nashit affirming an extra yāʾ, contrary to the rest of his transmitters; the source says others follow their established principles.
NASHR:v2p184/r4.anchor: وانفرد في المبهج بإثباتها عن أبي نشيط فخالف سائر الرواة عنه، وهم في الإثبات على أصولهم

NASHR:v2p184/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p184/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p184/r5.claim: They agree on affirming eight extra yāʾs, including واتقون, خافون, اخشون, وقد هدان, ثم كيدون, ولا تخزون, أشركتمون, and واتبعون, each according to their principles.
NASHR:v2p184/r5.anchor: واتفق أبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب على إثبات ثماني ياءات، وهي واتقون ياأولي الألباب في البقرة، وخافون إن في آل عمران

NASHR:v2p184/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p184/r6.speaker: هشام
NASHR:v2p184/r6.claim: The majority of authorities establish Hisham's yāʾ in ثم كيدون in both pause and continuation; Ibn al-Jazari follows that form and says the Taysir should be read accordingly.
NASHR:v2p184/r6.anchor: فقطع له الجمهور بالياء في الحالين، وهو الذي في الكافي والتبصرة

NASHR:v2p184/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p184/r7.speaker: هشام
NASHR:v2p184/r7.claim: Other transmitters report Hisham affirming the yāʾ in continuation but deleting it at pause.
NASHR:v2p184/r7.anchor: وروى الآخرون عنه الإثبات في الوصل دون الوقف

NASHR:v2p186/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p186/r2.speaker: ابن سوار وابن فارس
NASHR:v2p186/r2.claim: They agree on affirming خافون, اخشون, هدان, كيدون, and تخزون in both positions, and أشركتمون only in continuation.
NASHR:v2p186/r2.anchor: واتفق ابن سوار، وابن فارس على إثبات خافون، واخشون، وهدان، وكيدون، وتخزون في الحالين واتبعون على إثبات أشركتمون وصلا لا وقفا

NASHR:v2p186/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p186/r10.speaker: قنبل
NASHR:v2p186/r10.claim: The author introduces two further yāʾ locations in which Qunbul is distinctive, but the segment ends before listing them.
NASHR:v2p186/r10.anchor: واختص قنبل بإثبات الياء في موضعين، وهما

NASHR:v2p140/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p140/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p140/r11.claim: For alif deletion before a quiescent letter, the disputed case is the word أيه, occurring in three places; the segment does not yet detail those places.
NASHR:v2p140/r11.anchor: وأما ما حذف من الألفات لساكن فهو من المختلف فيه كلمة واحدة، وهي (أيه) وقعت في ثلاثة مواضع

QIRAAT-ER:7:195:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:9#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:9#1/r1.claim: Both kasra and ḍamma on ṭāʾ are valid Form I patterns; the ḍamma may sound heavier and more forceful.
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:9#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift: kasra→ḍamma on ṭāʾ (yabṭishūna→yabṭushūna); both are valid Form I patterns

QIRAAT-ER:7:195:23#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:23#1/r1.speaker: vhr
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:23#1/r1.claim: Before hamzat al-waṣl, qul may take liaison kasra or ḍamma; the latter preserves the imperative's original vowel while kasra assimilates to the liaison context.
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:23#1/r1.anchor: Liaison vowel variant: qul-i (kasra) vs qul-u (ḍamma) before hamzat al-waṣl of udʿū

QIRAAT-ER:7:195:27#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:27#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:27#1/r1.claim: The full yāʾ form explicitly restores the first person object pronoun that is otherwise implied by the nūn's kasra.
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:27#1/r1.anchor: Full yāʾ restoration: kīdūni→kīdūnī — the 1s object pronoun yāʾ is written explicitly

QIRAAT-ER:7:195:27#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:27#2/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:27#2/r1.claim: A pausal form with sukūn alternates with the continuous form retaining full yāʾ, reflecting recitation context.
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:27#2/r1.anchor: Pausal vs continuous variant: kīdūn (with sukūn, pausal) alternating with kīdūnī (full yāʾ, continuous)

QIRAAT-ER:7:195:30#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:30#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:30#1/r1.claim: The full yāʾ explicitly restores the first person pronoun otherwise implied by the nūn's kasra.
QIRAAT-ER:7:195:30#1/r1.anchor: Full yāʾ restoration: tunẓirūni→tunẓirūnī — explicit 1s pronoun yāʾ written rather than implied

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r3.claim: Al-baṭsh is taking or seizing with force.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r3.anchor: البطش الأخذ بقوة بطش يبطش بضم الطاء وكسرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r4.claim: The verb yabṭishu is also pronounced yabṭushu, with either kasra or ḍamma on ṭāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's claim that the following question cancels the likeness: likeness in creation or ownership remains, while the question belittles the idols' missing organs and uses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r7.anchor: وليس كما زعم لأنه تعالى حكم على هؤلاء المدعوين من دون الله أنهم عباد أمثال الداعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r8.claim: The question about organs cannot invalidate God's earlier statement; that would make one of two divine reports false, which is impossible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r8.anchor: وأيضا فالأبطال لا يتصور بالنسبة إليه تعالى لأنه يدل على كذب أحد الخبرين وذلك مستحيل بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r9.claim: Lacking useful organs does not negate likeness in being created or owned and subdued; the question instead shows idols are inferior to humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r9.anchor: وإنما ذلك تحقير لشأن الأصنام وأنهم دونكم في انتفاء الآلات التي أعدت للانتفاع بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r11.claim: The questions express denial and amazement, showing that idols are inert and lack the organs and functions for which such organs were made; humans are superior.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r11.anchor: هذا استفهام إنكار وتعجيب وتبيين أنهم جماد لا حراك لهم وأنهم فاقدون لهذه الأعضاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r12.claim: The negation can target the existence of the organs and their functions together, or target their functions even if the idols are sculpted with the organs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r12.anchor: قد يتوجه الإنكار فيه إلى انتفاء هذه الأعضاء وانتفاء منافعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r1.claim: Each disjunctive am means bal plus hamza, marking transition rather than cancellation and denying each capacity in turn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r1.anchor: وأم هنا منقطعة فتقدر ببل والهمزة وهو إضراب على معنى الانتقال لا على معنى الإبطال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r2.claim: The questions are ordered from the most important capacity downward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r2.anchor: وكان ترتيب هذه الجمل هكذا لأنه بدىء بالأهم ثم أتبع بما هو دونه إلى آخرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r3.speaker: الحسن والأعرج ونافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, and Nāfiʿ read the ṭāʾ in yabṭishūna with kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعرج ونافع بكسر الطاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, and Nāfiʿ also transmit a reading with ḍamma on ṭāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع بضمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī reports an argument that denying the idols' organs would imply that God also lacks divinity if He lacks such organs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: تعلق بعض الأغمار بهذه الآية في إثبات هذه الأعضاء لله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that humans have functional limbs while idols do not, making humans superior and worship of the inferior unreasonable; the verse also reiterates that idols cannot benefit or harm, while God has perfect power, hearing, and sight without bodily organs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r6.anchor: أن المقصود من الآية أن الإنسان أفضل وأكمل حالا من الصنم لأنه له رجل ماشية ويد باطشة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r7.claim: After showing that idols are inert, God commands the Prophet to invite them to do their worst: the challenge shows he fears neither them nor their worshippers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r7.anchor: أمر تعالى نبيه أن يقول لهم ذلك أي لا مبالاة بكم ولا بشركائكم فاصنعوا ما تشاؤون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r8.claim: Idʿū means seek their help; kīdūnī means plot to harm me; fa-lā tunẓirūn means do not delay what you intend.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r8.anchor: ومعنى ادعوا شركاءكم استعينوا بهم على إيصال الضر إلي ثم كيدون أي امكروا بي ولا تؤخرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r9.claim: They are called the idolaters' partners because the idolaters relate them to themselves by naming them gods and God's partners.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r9.anchor: وسمى الأصنام شركاءهم من حيث أن لهم نسبة إليهم بتسميتهم إياهم آلهة وشركاء الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r10.claim: The challenge echoes Hūd's reply to his people: call your alleged gods and plot against me without delay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r10.anchor: وهذا كما قال قوم هود إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو وهشام
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r11.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Hishām in one transmission retain the yāʾ in fa-kīdūnī in both connected and paused reading; the other seven readers omit it, relying on the kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p252/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وهشام بخلاف عنه فكيدوني بإثبات الياء وصلا ووقفا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r1.claim: The questions intensify the rebuke by showing the idols lack the faculties needed to answer the preceding challenge.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r1.anchor: تبكيت إثر تبكيت مؤكد لما يفيده الأمر التعجيزي من عدم الإستجابة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r2.claim: If likeness means actual equality, idols are inferior to humans, making their worship even less fitting; if likeness is hypothetical, the verse cancels that supposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r2.anchor: في المماثلة كر على المثلية بالنقض لأنهم أدون منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r3.claim: On the light, negative reading of inna, these questions further establish the idols’ incapacity and lack of likeness.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r3.anchor: وعلى قراءة التخفيف وإرادة النفي تقرير لنفي المماثلة بإثبات القصور والنقصان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r4.claim: Each of the four faculties is questioned separately to repeat the rebuke and show that absence of any one suffices to disprove the ability to answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r4.anchor: ووجه الإنكار إلى كل واحد من تلك الآلآت الأربع على حدة تكريرا للبكيت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r5.claim: The point is simply incapacity, not that possessing limbs is a condition of divinity; the verse does not deny God’s divinity or establish the corporealism claimed by some anthropomorphists.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r5.anchor: وليس المراد أن من لم يكن له هذه لا يستحق الألوهية وإنما يستحقها من كانت له

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r6.claim: The wording makes the leg’s function the target: since the idols show none of the characteristic action of real legs, they are not legs in reality; the same applies to the other organs.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r6.anchor: ووصفه الأرجل بالمشي بها للإيذان بأن مدار الإنكار هو الوصف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r7.claim: Am is disconnected here; its hamza continues the rebuke, while bal shifts from one completed mode of argument to another.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r7.anchor: منقطعة وما فيها من الهمزة لما مر من البكيت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r8.claim: Al-baṭsh means taking hold with force.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r9.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads yaṭbishūn with ḍamma on ṭāʾ, a dialectal form meaning to take what they want or defend you.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r10.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r10.claim: The hands follow the legs because walking describes the idols’ condition in themselves, whereas grasping describes their relation to others.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r10.anchor: كما قال شيخ الإسلام لما أن المشي حالهم في أنفسهم والبطش حالهم بالنسبة إلى الغير

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r11.claim: Hands precede eyes and ears to pair with legs and because lack of walking or grasping is more obvious and more forceful as a rebuke.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r11.anchor: ولأن انتفاء المشي والبطش أظهر والبكيت به أقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r12.claim: Eyes precede ears because they are more familiar and more evident in appearance and effect; seeing by eyes and hearing by ears are ordinary outward associations.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r12.anchor: فلأنها أشهر منها وأظهر عينا وأثرا وكون الإبصار بالعين والسماع بالأذن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r13.claim: The verse supports the view that God places in some things a power by which they have effects when He permits; al-Ālūsī rejects calling this near disbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r13.anchor: أودع في بعض الأشياء قوة بها تؤثر إذا أذن الله تعالى لها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r14.claim: The Prophet is told to confront the idolaters and renew the challenge after establishing that their partners can do nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r14.anchor: أمر له صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بأن يناصبهم المحاجة ويكرر عليهم البكيت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r15.claim: He challenges the idolaters and their partners to devise every possible plot against him without delay, expressing complete fearlessness.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144#2/r15.anchor: شركاءكم واستعينوا بهم علي ( ثم كيدون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p145/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p145/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p145/r1.claim: The two first-person yāʾs are omitted in the written form; Abū ʿAmr retains the yāʾ of kaydūn at connection, Hishām in both positions, and other readers omit it. In 11:55 all retain it in kaydūnī; al-Ajhūrī says tunẓirūnī always omits its yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p145/r1.anchor: وياء المتكلم في الفعلين مما لم يثبتوها خطا وقرأ أبو عمرو بإثبات ياء كيدون وصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r24.claim: The question denies that idols have legs to walk; God alone makes them walk, and the same interpretation applies to the other faculties.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r24.anchor: استفهام على سبيل الإنكار أي ليس لهم أرجل يمشون بها بل الله عز وجل إذ هو الذي يمشيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r1.claim: The inward challenge tells opponents to plot against the Prophet if they can, continuing the exposure of their alleged powerlessness.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r6.claim: The question about the idols’ limbs continues the argument that they cannot answer or benefit their worshippers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r6.anchor: ثم بين عجزهم فقال: {ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads the hāʾ in لهم with ḍamma here and in al-Qasas and al-Dukhan; the others read it with kasra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر بضم الهاء هنا وفي القصص والدخان، وقرأ الآخرون بكسر الطاء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r2.claim: Created beings act through limbs and senses, but idols lack them; people are superior and more capable, so worshipping idols is irrational.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r2.anchor: أراد أن قدرة المخلوقين تكون بهذه الجوارح والآلات، وليست للأصنام هذه الآلات، فأنتم مفضلون عليها بالأرجل الماشية والأيدي الباطشة والأعين الباصرة والآذان السامعة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r3.claim: The address is to the polytheists; “your partners” means the idols they associate with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r3.anchor: {قل ادعوا شركاءكم} يا معشر المشركين، {ثم كيدون} أنتم وهم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r4.claim: The challenge is for the polytheists and their idols to conspire against the Prophet.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r5.claim: فلا تنظرون means do not delay me; hurry to plot against me.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315#2/r5.anchor: {فلا تنظرون} أي: لا تمهلوني واعجلوا في كيدي.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r1.claim: A variant lightens inna and puts ʿibād in the accusative, treating the particle as a negation like Ḥijāzī mā; the author says this construction is unattested.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r1.anchor: بتخفيف { أن } ونصب { عباد } على أنها نافية

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r2.claim: Yabṭishūn is read with ḍamma here and in al-Qaṣaṣ and al-Dukhān.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r3.claim: He challenges them to summon their alleged partners and enlist them in hostility toward him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r3.anchor: ادعوا شركاءكم } واستعينوا بهم في عداوتي

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r4.claim: He challenges them to use every available stratagem without delay.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r4.anchor: فبالغوا فيما تقدرون عليه من مكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r5.claim: He fears nothing because he trusts in God’s guardianship and protection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:195/r5.anchor: فلا تمهلون فإني لا أبالي بكم لوثوقي

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r10.claim: The taunting questions proceed through movement, striking, sight, and hearing: movement is the first feared action, then assault, then seeing danger, then hearing a threat from afar or out of sight.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r10.anchor: مقدما الأجل لأن أول ما يخشى من الشيء انتقاله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r11.claim: Their failure to possess these capacities makes the idols inferior to humans and effectively nonexistent in themselves; any capacity they have is granted by their maker.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r11.anchor: لزم نقصانها عنهم وأنه في الحقيقة مسلوب عنهم لأنهم ليس لهم من ذواتهم إلا العدم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r12.claim: The Prophet challenges them and their partners together to plot against him, despite their multitude and his solitude, and not to delay even a moment.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r12.anchor: أي جميعا أنتم وهم وأنتم أكثر من حصى البطحاء ورمل الفضاء وأنا وحدي

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r1.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r1.claim: Salman distinguishes a covered heart belonging to a disbeliever from an inverted heart belonging to a hypocrite.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r1.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي قال : القلوب اربعة ، قلب اغلف فذلك قلب الكافر وقلب منكوس فذلك قلب المنافق

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r2.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r2.claim: A heart containing both faith and hypocrisy is one of the four types Salman describes.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r2.anchor: وقلب مصفح فذاك قلب فيه ايمانه ونفاق

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r3.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r3.claim: Salman describes the believer's heart as bare, containing a lamp whose light is its radiance.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r3.anchor: وقلب اجرد فيه سراج وسراجه نوره وذلك قلب المؤمن

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r4.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r4.claim: Faith is like a plant watered with water and hypocrisy like a sore watered with pus; whichever prevails consumes its host until God determines its end.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636#2/r4.anchor: فمثل الايمان كمثل البقلة يسقيها الماء ، ومثل النفاق فيه كمثل القرحة يسقيها الصديد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r1.claim: The questions confirm the preceding challenge: lacking the means of response makes the idols’ incapacity certain and intensifies the challenge against both idols and worshippers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r1.anchor: تأكيد لما تضمنته الجملة قبلها من أمر التعجيز وثبوت العجز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r2.claim: The interrogative is condemnatory; fronting the predicate stresses the absence of possession marked by the lām, as in Ḥassān’s line about unmatched ambitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r2.anchor: كالتقديم في قول حسان : له همم لا منتهى لكبارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r3.claim: The organ descriptions either intensify the record of incapacity where aid is needed or address idols made in human form, such as Hubal, Dhū al-Kaffayn, Kaʿb, and the female-form Suwāʿ; their organs cannot function.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r3.anchor: مثل هبل ، وذي الكفين ، وكعيب في صور الرجال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r4.claim: These four organs are means of knowledge, movement, and defensive aid; tongues are omitted because the invocation seeks rescue, and rescuers rush without asking why help is needed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r4.anchor: وخص الأرجل والأيدي والأعين والآذان ، لأنها آلات العلم والسعي والدفع للنصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r5.claim: Walking is the feet’s repeated movement from one place to another; batsh is forceful taking or harming by hand.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r5.anchor: والمشي انتقال الرجلين من موضع انتقالا متواليا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r6.claim: The imperfect of batsh has both kasra and ḍamma in the ṭāʾ; the majority read with kasra and Abū Jaʿfar with ḍamma, both recognized forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r6.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور بالكسر ، وقرأ أبو جعفر : بضم الطاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r7.claim: Am coordinates interrogatives like aw and can offer alternatives, distinguish between options, or permit combining them; after a genuine question seeking specification, it has the force of a choice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r7.anchor: وهي تكون مثل ( أو ) لأحد الشيئين أو الأشياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r8.claim: After a nonliteral question, disconnected am means permissive aw or transitional bal, while still implying a question; here each clause means, ‘rather, do they have…?’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p222/r8.anchor: وإن وقعت بعد استفهام غير حقيقي كانت بمعنى ( أو ) التي للإباحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r1.claim: The limbs are ordered by their usefulness in rescue: feet rush to the caller, hands perform the fighting, and eyes and ears serve as means for both; eyes precede ears here, unlike the usual Qurʾanic order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r1.anchor: وترتيب هذه الجوارح الأربع على حسب ما في الآية ملحوظ فيه أهميتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r2.claim: God authorizes the Prophet to challenge the polytheists to summon their idols and combine against him for their aid, so they can be rid of him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r2.anchor: إذن من الله لرسوله بأن يتحداهم بأنهم إن استطاعوا استصرخوا أصنامهم لتتألب على الكيد للرسول عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r3.claim: Kayd means harm made to appear harmless, as explained earlier in 7:183.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r3.anchor: والكيد الإضرار الواقع في صورة عدم الإضرار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r4.claim: Both the command to plot and the prohibition against delaying are challenge forms meant to show the opponents’ inability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223/r4.anchor: والأمر والنهي في قوله : { كيدون فلا تنظرون } للتعجيز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r1.speaker: author
