IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r1.claim: Do not give me respite follows from the challenge: if they can harm him, they should do it at once rather than delay.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r1.anchor: تفريع على الأمر بالكيد ، أي فإذا تمكنتم من اضراري فأعجلوا ولا تؤجلوني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r2.claim: The challenge hints that the Prophet will triumph and destroy their idols; it gives them the fullest conditions for victory—powerful allies, secret harm, and no delay—so failure proves their impotence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r2.anchor: وفي هذا التحدي تعريض بأنه سيبلغهم وينتصر عليهم ويستأصل آلهتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r3.claim: Most readers except Abū ʿAmr omit the speaker’s yāʾ from kaydūn in both pausing and continuation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r3.anchor: في قراءة الجمهور غير أبي عمرو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r4.claim: All readers except Yaʿqūb omit the yāʾ in tanẓirūn; Yaʿqūb retains it in both pause and continuation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r4.anchor: فقرأه الجميع : بحذف الياء إلا يعقوب أثبتها وصلا ووقفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r5.claim: Dropping the speaker’s yāʾ after the protective nūn is highly eloquent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p223#2/r5.anchor: وحذف ياء المتكلم بعد نون الوقاية جد فصيح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r9.claim: The questions ask whether idols have the senses and capacities of living creatures; denying these details forces assent to the broader conclusion that they are inert.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r9.anchor: الغرض من هذه الآية، ألهم حواس الحي وأوصافه؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r10.claim: Breaking the general claim into specific faculties makes the proof stronger and leaves no room for doubt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r10.anchor: فإذا وقع الإقرار بتفصيلات القضية لزم الإقرار بعمومها وكان بيانها أقوى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r11.speaker: الزهراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r11.claim: Al-Zahrawī says the worshippers themselves are superior to the idols because they possess useful limbs, so they should not worship them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r11.anchor: قال الزهراوي: المعنى أنتم أفضل منهم بهذه الجوارح النافعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r2.claim: Each am in the questions turns away from the preceding clause; it is not the alternative am paired with alif when asking which of two things is present.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r2.anchor: وقوله في الآية أم إضراب لكل واحدة عن الجملة المتقدمة لها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r3.claim: The author calls the distinction semantic; in wording and grammatical analysis, both kinds of am are the same.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r3.anchor: وهذا عندي فرق معنوي، وأما من جهة اللفظ والصناعة النحوية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r4.speaker: نافع والحسن والأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, al-Ḥasan, and al-Aʿraj read yabṭishūna with kasra on the ṭāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع والحسن والأعرج «يبطشون» بكسر الطاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r5.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر وشيبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r5.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū Jaʿfar, and Shayba also transmit yabṭushūna with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع أيضا وأبو جعفر وشيبة «يبطشون» بضمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r6.claim: God commands the Prophet to challenge them to summon the idols to harm or plot against him, and not delay; if they are gods, their action should become evident.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r6.anchor: ثم أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يعجزهم بقوله قل ادعوا شركاءكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r7.claim: They are called “partners” because the people assigned them a relation to themselves by naming them gods and partners of God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r7.anchor: وسماهم شركاءهم من حيث لهم نسبة إليهم بتسميتهم إياهم آلهة وشركاء لله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ retain the yāʾ in kaydūnī when connecting the words.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونافع «كيدوني» بإثبات الياء في الوصل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r9.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī omit the yāʾ in both connection and pause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «كيدون» بحذف الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r10.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r10.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains that yāʾ deletion is common when speech resembles a separate phrase or a rhyme, as in al-Aʿshā’s verse ending with an omitted yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي: إذا أشبه الكلام المنفصل أو كان منفصلا أشبه القافية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r11.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r11.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line “أن يأتين” illustrates omission of the final yāʾ in rhyme.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r11.anchor: كما قال الأعشى: [المتقارب] فهل يمنعني ارتيادي البلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r12.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r12.claim: A second al-Aʿshā line, “يلمس الأحلاس,” illustrates omission of the yāʾ that marks the imperative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r12.anchor: كما قال الأعشى: [الرمل] يلمس الأحلاس في منزله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r13.claim: Falayunẓirūn means “do not delay me”; the author links it with the same sense of naẓara in 2:280.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r13.anchor: وقوله فلا تنظرون أي لا تؤخرون، ومنه قوله تعالى: فنظرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r1.claim: The question asks whether idols have legs to walk with and pursue their interests.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r1.anchor: في المصالح ﴿ أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r2.claim: The question asks whether idols have hands to strike with and repel harm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r2.anchor: في المصالح ﴿ أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها ﴾ في دفع ما يؤذي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r3.claim: The question asks whether idols have eyes to distinguish benefits from harms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r3.anchor: المنافع من المضار ﴿ أم لهم آذان يسمعون بها ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r4.claim: The question asks whether idols have ears to hear worshippers' pleading and prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r4.anchor: تضرعكم ودعاءكم وفي هذا تنبيه على تفضيل العابدين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r5.claim: The questions show worshippers are superior to the worshipped and rebuke people for worshipping beings inferior to themselves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r5.anchor: وفي هذا تنبيه على تفضيل العابدين على المعبودين وتوبيخ لهم حيث عبدوا من هم أفضل منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says Meccan unbelievers threatened the Prophet with their idols, so God challenged them to call their partners.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن كانوا يخوفونه بآلهتهم فقال الله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r7.claim: The challenge to plot against the Prophet is addressed to the idolaters and their idols together.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r7.anchor: ادعوا شركاءكم ثم كيدون ﴾ أنتم وهم ﴿ فلا تنظرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r8.claim: The command means do not delay or give respite.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r8.anchor: ﴿ فلا تنظرون ﴾ أي لا تؤخروا ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r9.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i omit the yāʾ in kaydūn in connected and paused reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r9.anchor: وكان ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي يقرؤون ثم كيدون بغير ياء في الوصل والوقف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r10.claim: Abu Amr and Nafi, in Ibn Hammad's transmission, retain the yāʾ in connected reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونافع في رواية ابن حماد بالياء في الوصل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r11.speaker: ورش وقالون والمسيبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r11.claim: Warsh, Qalun, and al-Musayyibi omit the yāʾ in connected reading and at pause.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r11.anchor: وروى ورش وقالون والمسيبي بغير ياء في الوصل ولا وقف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r12.speaker: يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r12.claim: Ya'qub retains the yāʾ in tanẓurūn in connected and paused reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306#2/r12.anchor: فأما تنظرون فأثبت فيها الياء يعقوب في الوصل والوقف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r4.claim: The questions about legs, hands, eyes, and ears expose that the supposed partners cannot move, grasp, see, or hear and therefore cannot act as gods.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r4.anchor: بل الأناسي أكمل منها، لأنها تسمع وتبصر وتبطش، وتلك لا تفعل شيئا من ذلك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r5.claim: The challenge means: call your partners to help against me, scheme with all your force, and do not delay me even a moment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r5.anchor: وقوله: {قل ادعوا شركاءكم ثم كيدون فلا تنظرون}

JISHUMI:v4p2813/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r11.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Nafiʿ, and Abu ʿAmr retain the yāʾ in kīdūnī; the other readers omit it.
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r11.anchor: أثبت الياء في قوله: كيدوني أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو، والباقون بحذفها،

JISHUMI:v4p2813/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r12.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r12.claim: Yaʿqub retains the yāʾ in tunẓirūn, while the other readers omit it.
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r12.anchor: وأثبت يعقوب الياء في تنظرون وحذفها الآخرون،

JISHUMI:v4p2813/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r13.claim: Retaining the yāʾ follows the original form; omitting it lightens pronunciation, with the context making the omitted letter understood.
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r13.anchor: فالإثبات على الأصل والحذف للتخفيف، مع دلالة الكلام عليه.

JISHUMI:v4p2813/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r14.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads yabṭushūn with ḍamma on ṭāʾ, as also in al-Qasas and al-Dukhan; the other readers use kasra.
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r14.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر يبطشون بضم الطاء، وكذلك في (القصص) و(الدخان).

JISHUMI:v4p2813/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r17.claim: Baṭsh means taking or seizing; the related phrase ‘a seizing by the Lord’ is cited as usage.
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r17.anchor: والبطش: الأخذ، ويد باطشة، ومنه: (إن بطش ربك لشديد).

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r5.claim: He challenges them to summon their partners for help against him and plot together without delay; only one confident of God’s protection could speak this way, since they had threatened him with their idols.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r5.anchor: استعينوا بهم في عدوني { ثم كيدون } جميعا أنتم وشركاؤكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r6.claim: The challenge echoes Hūd’s response after his people claimed their gods had harmed him: he declared himself free of their gods and challenged them to plot without delay.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r6.anchor: قوم هود له : { إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض ءالهتنا بسوء }

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r1.claim: The questions refer to idols, which lack limbs with which to serve their worshippers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r1.anchor: يعني أرجل يمشون بها في مصالحكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r2.claim: The idols cannot walk to attend to their worshippers’ interests.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r2.anchor: يعني أرجل يمشون بها في مصالحكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r3.claim: The idols lack hands with which to defend their worshippers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r4.claim: The idols cannot see their worshippers’ harms and benefits.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r5.claim: The idols cannot hear worshippers’ calls and supplications.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r6.claim: Worshipping a body that cannot benefit anyone is more blameworthy than worshipping one that can.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r6.anchor: أن من عبد جسما لا ينفع كان ألوم ممن عبد جسما ينفع

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p287/r7.claim: People are superior to idols, so it is incoherent for them to worship beings beneath them.

MUQATIL:7:190-197/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r11.claim: The rhetorical questions expose that the idols lack the bodily faculties of walking, grasping, seeing, and hearing.
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r11.anchor: { ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها أم لهم أعين يبصرون بها أم لهم آذان يسمعون بها }

MUQATIL:7:190-197/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r12.claim: The Prophet challenges the Meccans and their idols to call their partners and plot against him together without delay.
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r12.anchor: ثم قال لكفار مكة: { قل ادعوا شركاءكم } ، يعنى الآلهة، { ثم كيدون } أنتم الآلهة جميعا بشر، { فلا تنظرون }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r1.claim: The questions show idols lack the worshippers’ ability to walk, grasp, see, or hear, so it is irrational to worship beings inferior to them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r1.anchor: الأعراف 185 190 ﴿ أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها ﴾ يتناولون بها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r2.claim: The Prophet is told to summon the idols for aid in opposing him.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r3.claim: He challenges the idolaters and their idols to plot against him together.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r4.speaker: يعقوب وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb reads with yāʾ, and Abū ʿAmr agrees when continuing recitation.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r4.anchor: بالياء يعقوب وافقه أبو عمرو فى الوصل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r5.claim: «Do not give me respite» means he does not care about them; they had threatened him with their idols, so he was ordered to challenge them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#5/r5.anchor: فانى لا أبالى بكم وكانوا قد خوفوه ى لهتم فأمر أن يخاطبهم بذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r10.claim: God rebukes them: people are superior to idols, so it is foolish to worship them; an object of worship ought to possess bodily faculties.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r10.anchor: أي أنتم أفضل منهم فكيف تعبدونهم. والغرض بيان جهلهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r16.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r16.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Shaybah read yabṭishūna with a ḍamma on ṭāʾ; this is a dialect form.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r16.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة { أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها } بضم الطاء، وهي لغة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r17.claim: Hand, foot, and ear are feminine nouns and take tāʾ in diminutives; yad adds yāʾ in the diminutive to restore its root, yielding yadiyyah with doubled yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r17.anchor: واليد والرجل والأذن مؤنثات يصغرن بالهاء. وتزاد في اليد ياء في التصغير

BURSEVI:v3p226/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226/r5.claim: Bodily response requires life, a mover, and moving and perceiving faculties; beings lacking all of these cannot act, and the walking predicate is the focus of the denial.
BURSEVI:v3p226/r5.anchor: إنما تتصور إذا كان لها محرك حياة وقوى محركة ومدركة

BURSEVI:v3p226/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226/r6.claim: The wording stresses walking with the legs because the negation turns on the asserted action, walking.
BURSEVI:v3p226/r6.anchor: ووصف الأرجل بالمشي بها للإيذان بأن مدار الإنكار هو الوصف

BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r1.claim: The disconnected am is understood as bal plus a hamza; batsh means taking something with force.
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r1.anchor: أم منقطعة مقدرة ببل والهمزة والبطش الأخذ بقوة

BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r2.claim: The question asks whether the idols have hands with which to seize what they want; bal shifts to a new mode of rebuke after the previous one is complete.
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r2.anchor: بل للإضراب المفيد للانتقال من فن من التبكيت بعد تمامه إلى فن آخر منه

BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r3.claim: Walking comes first as the idols’ condition in themselves; grasping is their condition in relation to others.
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r3.anchor: قدم المشي لأنه حالهم في أنفسهم والبطش حالهم بالنسبة إلى الغير

BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r4.claim: Hands precede eyes to pair hands with legs; eyes precede ears because they are more familiar and more manifest in sight and effect.
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r4.anchor: وأما تقديم الأعين فلما أنها أشهر من الآذان وأظهر عينا وأثرا

BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r5.claim: The idolaters threatened the Prophet with harm from their gods; God challenges them and their idols to plot against him with all their power.
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r5.anchor: ثم إن الكفار كانوا يخوفونه عليه السلام بآلهتهم قائلين نخاف

BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r6.claim: He tells them not to delay even an hour, confident that God will protect and guard him.
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r6.anchor: فلا تمهلون ساعة فإني لا أبالي بكم لوثوقي على ولاية الله وحفظه

BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r7.claim: The Persian couplet voices fearless reliance on God as protector even if both worlds unite against the speaker.
BURSEVI:v3p226#2/r7.anchor: اكر هر دو جهانم خصم كردند نترسم ون نكهبا نم تو باشى

RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r1.claim: The four organs matter insofar as they possess the powers of motion and perception: humans exceed lifeless idols, so it is unfitting for the superior to worship an inferior that can neither benefit nor protect.
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r1.anchor: فكيف يليق بالأفضل الأكمل الأشرف أن يشتغل بعبادة الأخس الأدون الذي لا يحس منه فائدة البتة

RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r2.speaker: المشبهة
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r2.claim: Some crude anthropomorphists argue that because lacking bodily organs proves idols are not divine, God must possess those organs or likewise lack divinity.
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r2.anchor: تعلق بعض أغمار المشبهة وجها لهم بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r3.claim: Rāzī rejects that inference: the verse compares the functional human body with the inert idol to establish human superiority; that comparison is its purpose, not an affirmation of organs for God.
RAZI-FULL:v15p75#2/r3.anchor: فهذا هو المقصود من ذكر هذا الكلام

RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r1.claim: The verse reinforces the preceding proof that idols cannot help their worshippers or themselves: lacking moving limbs and perceiving senses, they cannot benefit or harm, unlike God, who transcends bodily organs yet has perfect power, hearing, and sight.
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r1.anchor: الحجة التي ذكرها قبل هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the idolaters used to threaten the Messenger with their gods; the challenge invites them to summon and plot with the idols so their inability to harm him becomes clear.
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r2.anchor: قال الحسن : إنهم كانوا يخوفون الرسول عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r3.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retain the yāʾ in kīdūnī, while the other readers omit it.
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r3.anchor: وأثبت نافع وأبو عمرو الياء في

RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r4.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains the omitted yāʾ by saying verse endings resemble rhymes and Arabic poetry also drops such yāʾs at line ends, citing a verse as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r4.anchor: قال الواحدي ، والقول فيه أن الفواصل تشبه القوافي

RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r5.claim: Those who retain the yāʾ follow the original form.
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r5.anchor: والذين أثبتوها فلأن الأصل هو الإثبات

RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r6.claim: “Do not give me respite” means do not delay; the idolaters and their partners are told to hurry their plot.
RAZI-FULL:v15p76/r6.anchor: أي لا تمهلوني واعجلوا في كيدي أنتم وشركائكم
